as_told.title: Harold Malmgren flagged to the CIA and 'the Majestic' after writing to the Atomic Energy Commission

plain: Harald Malmgren, who later advised several US presidents on trade, says that as a young man in the 1950s his name went into secret lists of talent kept not only by the CIA, the US spy agency, but by "the Majestic," a group he calls guardians who took it on themselves to protect the world's secrets. In his own interview he ties this to the day he met Karl Compton, the president of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and also mentions Christian Herter, then a senior US statesman. When Michels retells it in a later episode, he says the flagging followed a letter Malmgren wrote to the Atomic Energy Commission, the agency then in charge of nuclear work, which would mean a hidden body was watching for gifted young people from the start.
